title: The community seed archive
paragraphs: At the edge of the town library stood a cabinet of dormant seeds collected from farms that no longer operated. Although the seeds were inactive, some could still grow if stored under suitable conditions.
Many envelopes carried ambiguous labels such as ‘red bean, upper field’. Without a year or farmer's name, the description was difficult to connect to a particular crop.
Student volunteers made a meticulous inventory. They copied every mark, photographed torn labels and kept uncertain words inside square brackets rather than guessing.
Their first catalogue was provisional. It helped the team organise interviews, but no entry was treated as final until another source supported it.
Several details were later corroborated by farm maps and family notebooks. The archive did not recover every missing fact, yet it preserved a transparent boundary between evidence and inference.
